skill.description: Generate text-to-video clips with HappyHorse 1.0 through the RunComfy CLI. The skill documents supported video settings, prompt guidance, RunComfy account requirements, and security notes for token storage and downloads.

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally uses the RunComfy CLI to submit text-to-video jobs and download generated outputs. Most static findings are Markdown formatting, examples, URLs, or documented service behavior rather than hidden execution, path traversal, or reconnaissance. The remaining confirmed issues are disclosed external command and network dependencies that users should understand before installing.

remediation.issue: External CLI dependency executes locally and may install third-party code.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the command arguments fixed, document the exact package source, and require user confirmation before installation or generation runs.

remediation.issue: Prompts and bearer tokens are sent to the RunComfy Model API.
remediation.suggestion: State clearly that user prompts leave the local machine and advise users not to include secrets or private data in prompts.

remediation.issue: Generated assets are downloaded to a user-selected output directory.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend an explicit project output directory and keep the documented host allowlist and file-size cap in place.

content.value_statement: Creating short AI videos often requires exact model settings and repeatable prompts. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through HappyHorse 1.0 generation with RunComfy.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to choose HappyHorse 1.0 for text-to-video generation.
Documents the RunComfy CLI command for the HappyHorse text-to-video endpoint.
Lists supported aspect ratios, durations, resolutions, seeds, and watermark settings.
Provides prompt guidance for motion, camera direction, audio, and multi-shot consistency.
Describes RunComfy login, token storage, polling, downloads, and exit codes.
limitations: Requires a RunComfy account and local RunComfy CLI installation.
Supports only the documented text-to-video endpoint, not the image-to-video pipeline.
Video duration is limited to 3 through 15 seconds per generation.
Prompts and generation requests are processed by RunComfy, not fully locally.

use_cases.title: Create short brand videos
use_cases.description: Generate consistent character clips with camera direction, audio cues, and native 1080p output.

use_cases.title: Prototype cinematic scenes
use_cases.description: Test concise motion prompts, aspect ratios, and seeds before committing to a final video concept.

use_cases.title: Automate video generation from an IDE
use_cases.description: Use Claude Code or Codex to prepare RunComfy CLI commands for repeatable text-to-video jobs.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a basic clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Use HappyHorse 1.0 to generate a 5 second 16:9 1080p clip of a calm forest path at sunrise.

prompt_templates.title: Create a vertical social video
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 9:16 HappyHorse video for a coffee shop ad. Make it 8 seconds with warm cafe ambience and no watermark.

prompt_templates.title: Build a multi-shot scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Use HappyHorse 1.0 for a two-shot scene with the same character, wardrobe, and location details repeated in each shot.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a production-ready generation
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft the RunComfy HappyHorse command for a 1080p 15 second video with a fixed seed, clear audio direction, and a safe output directory.

output_examples.input: Generate a short product teaser for a travel backpack.
output_examples.output: A concise HappyHorse prompt with motion, camera angle, duration, aspect ratio, and audio notes for a polished product clip.

output_examples.input: Make a vertical ad with one actor in two scenes.
output: A multi-shot prompt that repeats character anchors.

output_examples.input: Explain why my RunComfy job failed with exit code 77.
output_examples.output: A plain-language explanation that the token is missing or rejected, plus the next login or token setup step.

best_practices: Use one clear motion beat per clip when iterating.
Repeat character and wardrobe anchors in every shot for consistency.
Use 720p and short duration for test passes before final 1080p renders.
anti_patterns: Do not paste secrets or private data into video prompts.
Do not request unsupported aspect ratios or durations outside 3 through 15 seconds.
Do not use vague still-image descriptions when the goal is motion.

faq.question: Does this skill generate video locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the local RunComfy CLI to send jobs to the RunComfy Model API.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What model endpoint does it target?
Can it create image-to-video outputs?
faq.answer: No. This skill documents the text-to-video endpoint only.

faq.question: Where is the RunComfy token stored?
faq.answer: The skill says runcomfy login stores it under ~/.config/runcomfy/token.json with owner-only permissions.

faq.question: What should I provide in a prompt?
faq.answer: Describe motion over time, camera framing, style, audio direction, and any character anchors.
